question.leadin: While this country existed, it surprisingly boasted the 4th-largest army in the world.
question.text: Name this multi-ethnic Balkan nation that lasted from its creation after World War I until its dissolution beginning in 1991. It was notably a Communist nation that remained outside of the Soviet sphere.
question.answerHtml: Yugoslavia [accept the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes]
question.clue: This country's Partisans were led by a man who once sent a threatening letter to another world leader reading, "if you don't stop sending killers , I'll send one to Moscow."

swap.text: Archduke Franz Ferdinand survived the first grenade thrown at his carriage, but a wrong turn after visiting those hurt in the blast at the hospital took him right by this Black Hand member eating lunch, who shot him on the second try.
swap.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

question.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
question.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Benito Mussolini.
swap.text: In 1939, Mussolini ordered the Italian army to attack this country ruled by King Zog before the start of World War II. Mussolini later used it as a beachhead to attack Greece and Yugoslavia in WWII.
swap.clue: Italy invaded this country during World War II when it was ruled by a man who claimed descent from Skanderbeg.

question.leadin: In 1981, a leader of this country banned typewriters because he feared citizens were using them to write messages to foreign embassies detailing the conditions in his country.
question.text: Name this country whose dictator Nicolae Ceausescu declared contraception illegal under Decree 770 in an attempt to increase this country's population.
question.clue: A ruler of this country embraced a "mini-Cultural Revolution" as part of a return to socialist realism in the July Theses.

swap.leadin: This region names two wars fought by a namesake league at the start of the 20th century, which involved Austrian intervention and Russian support.
swap.text: Name this region, the "powder keg of Europe," where Otto von Bismarck predicted the next European war would begin. A war ending in 1878 had ensured the independence of most of its states from a declining empire.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Bucharest resolved two namesake wars fought on this peninsula in 1912 and 1913, which the Ottoman Empire lost.

question.leadin: Basil II had the longest reign of any leader of his empire, revitalizing it over his nearly 50-year rule.
question.text: Basil is known as the "slayer" of this ethnic group for ending their first empire at the Battle of Kleidion in 1014 and having 99 of every 100 prisoners fully blinded and the remaining left with one eye.
question.answerHtml: Bulgars [do not accept or prompt on “Bulgarians,” as that is a distinct modern ethnic group]
question.clue: The Paulicians may have inspired a Gnostic, dualistic sect which arose among these people called Bogomilism.

swap.leadin: This country's Prime Minister Fan Noli came to power after the June Revolution.
swap.text: Name this Balkan country that was occupied by Italy from 1939 to 1943.
swap.clue: This home of Skanderbeg was ruled by the isolationist Enver Hoxha.

question.leadin: The army of the losing nation in the first of these conflicts was able to make a stand at Chataldzha and save its capital.
question.text: Identify this series of conflicts, the second of which began over border disputes in Macedonia.
question.clue: The first of these was ended by the Treaty of London, though it left the possession of Salonika and Thrace unresolved.

swap.text: In 1931, this king of Albania was almost killed while visiting Vienna to watch a performance of the opera Pagliacci. He was exiled from Albania when the country was annexed by Italy annexed in 1939.
swap.clue: He went into exile after Italy overran his country in 1939, abandoning the republican government he had formed in 1922.

question.leadin: While a circus acrobat named Otto Witte claimed to have briefly attained this position by impersonating the nephew of the Ottoman sultan, no one mentioned in his story exists to corroborate his account.
question.text: Name this position. Its only legitimate holder underwent 55 assassination attempts motivated by blood feuds, including one in which he returned with his own pistol after an attempt on his life at a showing of Pagliacci.
question.answerHtml: king of Albania [prompt on ruler of Albania; do not accept or prompt on “president of Albania” or “prime minister of Albania”] (The king is Zog I.)

swap.text: This Albanian hero left the Ottomans at the Battle of Nis. He later led his namesake rebellion against the Ottoman Empire, and also helped the Venetians in the First Ottoman-Venetian war before his death.
swap.clue: The Rilindja period of literary flourishment drew from that biography of this "Prince of the Epirotes" by Marin Barleti.

question.text: This statesman became head of state in 1967. Banning all abortion, he also issued the July Theses, which sought to improve the political-ideoligical activity of all working people, but he more famously was executed with his wife Elena in 1989.
question.clue: This man held back his country from participating in the Warsaw Pact invasion of Prague.

swap.leadin: During the Log Revolution, people native to one of these two modern-day countries constructed blockades made of logs in the other, rejecting changes made after a 1990 election.
swap.text: Name these two former members of Yugoslavia. Paramilitary units from one of them perpetrated the Vukovar Massacre in the other.
swap.answerHtml: Serbia and Croatia [or Republic of Serbia and Republic of Croatia; accept Republika Hrvatska in place of “Croatia”; accept Republika Srbija in place of “Serbia”; do not accept answers mentioning “Republika Srpska,” because that’s different]

question.leadin: As the Nazis swept through Europe, many puppet states sprang up in various occupied territories.
question.text: A puppet state in this modern-day country was led by the Poglavnik Ante Pavelic inside of Nazi-occupied Yugoslavia.
question.clue: The Duke of Aosta was appointed as the monarch of this country under the name (+) Tomislav II despite never setting foot in this country.

swap.leadin: According to angry Serbian nationalists on Youtube, this dynasty's king Uros the Weak was appropriately named, because he "did not kill Muslim, he did not kill foreigners."
swap.text: Name this major Serbian dynasty of the Middle Ages, which lasted from 1166 to 1371.
swap.clue: Stefan Dusan was a ruler from this Serbian dynasty, which lasted from 1166 to 1371. Founded in the principality of Raska by its namesake, its ruler Stefan the First-Crowned was recognized as king by Pope Honorius III while his brother Rastko was the first archbishop of an independent Serbian Orthodox Church.

question.leadin: Many of these institutions in Guatemala were closed after a fire at one called Hogar Seguro left 41 people dead.
question.text: Name these institutions. In the early 1990s, the 20/20 program "Shame of a Nation" called attention to the horrible state of these institutions in Romania.
question.answerHtml: orphanages [or children’s homes; prompt on care homes; reject “foster homes”]
question.clue: This type of institution run by the Salzburger emigrants. Dissatisfied with the standards of institutions of this type, Charles Loring Brace operated a controversial "Train Movement" to supplant them.

swap.leadin: Jason Vuic profiled Malcolm Bricklin's import of this product to America after five-hundred some alterations to reach US standards in a book about "The Rise and Fall" of this product.
swap.text: Give this brand name of notoriously shoddy imports that were sold in their homeland as Korals. This product's production was crippled by a 1999 NATO bombing of a facility mistaken for Zastava's arms factory.
swap.answerHtml: Yugos [or the Zastava Yugo; or the Yugo Koral; accept the Yugo GV; accept The Yugo: The Rise and Fall of the Worst Car in History]

question.text: According to tradition, this was the name of the Serbian soldier that assassinated the sultan Murad. He is venerated as a saint in the Serbian church and is celebrated in the epic poem The Mountain Wreath.
question.clue: Unfortunately for Murad, he was assassinated by this Serbian national hero toward the end of that very same Battle of Kosovo.

swap.text: The Ottomans captured Mihailovic at the silver-mining fortress of Novo Brdo ("BRR-doh") founded by this ruler. This ruler, who was canonized as the "Saint King," blinded a son who founded Visoki Decani monastery.
swap.answerHtml: Stefan Milutin [or Stefan Uroš II; or Uroš II Milutin Nemanjić; prompt on Stefan Uroš or Stefan Uroš or Nemanjić] (His son was Stefan Dečanski, or Stefan Uroš III.)
